resources.string: Share your phone screen securely or view another screen
Scan the EasyConnect QR code shown on the computer or the other phone
To share your screen, scan the QR code shown on the computer (EasyConnect → "App") or on another phone ("View another phone\'s screen").
Stop the current sharing session first.
Type with the keyboard (except password fields)
When banking, payment or password apps open, the video stops and control is blocked. Only you can allow them on this phone.
Files, photos, messages, contacts and passwords cannot be taken. Settings, permission screens and this app can\'t be controlled remotely.
Sharing pauses when the phone locks; the lock screen is never shown.
You can pause or stop from the notification at any time.
The connection is encrypted and goes only to this device.

EasyConnect: only during a sharing session you allowed, performs the other side\'s touches and text on this phone. Recognizes and hides banking and other protected apps. It doesn\'t read screen content or send it anywhere.
To allow control, turn on the "EasyConnect" service in Accessibility settings.

Remote control requires turning on the EasyConnect service in Android once:

1. Settings → Accessibility → Downloaded apps → EasyConnect
2. Turn it on and confirm.

If the switch is greyed out (the app isn't from the Play Store): Settings → Apps → EasyConnect → ⋮ at the top right → "Allow restricted settings", then try again.

The service only acts during a sharing session you allowed.
Setting up an encrypted connection with %1$s.
%1$s can see and control your screen.
%1$s can see and control your screen.
This is a protected app. %1$s can\'t see or control it. Show it? (Control stays blocked.)
%1$s tried to open a protected app. It was closed and nothing was shown.
When a checked app opens during sharing, the video stops and control is blocked. Banking and payment apps are checked automatically. (Requires the Accessibility service.)
Scan this QR code with EasyConnect on the other phone.
1. Both phones on the same Wi-Fi (or one connected to the other\'s hotspot).\n2. On the other phone: EasyConnect → "Share my screen — scan QR".\n3. That phone\'s owner chooses what to allow.
This phone isn\'t on any local network. Connect to Wi-Fi or turn on the hotspot, then tap "New QR".
The phone is locked — the lock screen is not shown.
A protected app is open (e.g. banking). It isn\'t shown without the phone owner\'s permission.
Control is allowed, but the service isn\'t on for that phone
This isn\'t an EasyConnect QR code.
This QR code is for a different app version. Update the app.
The QR code has no address.
Security: you can only connect to a device on the local network.
The QR code has an invalid port.
Screen sharing permission was not granted.
The QR code has expired or was already used. Create a new QR and scan again.
The other side closed the session.
Phone is locked — no video is sent.
Paused — the other side sees nothing.
Security: the other side\'s identity doesn\'t match the QR code, so we didn\'t connect. Only scan QR codes from your own devices.
Could not establish an encrypted connection. Create a new QR.
Could not connect (%1$s). If the other side changed networks, create a new QR and scan again. Both devices must be on the same Wi-Fi (or hotspot).
This version is view-only. To control the phone from a computer, use Developer mode (scrcpy) or the Google Play version of EasyConnect.
Banking and payment apps hide their own screens (they appear black). Nothing can be controlled remotely in this version.
Phone sound (music, video, games — not the microphone)
Change what the other side may do. This screen can\'t be controlled remotely.
Send a file to the other side
File transfer is not allowed in this session.
Tap to choose which file to send.
